title: AI labs reveal attacks being done on their own models, and debate industry slowdown - TCR 09/11/26
description:
Anthropic published a 154-page threat report detailing attempts to turn Claude toward bioweapons, three missile programs, and mass surveillance, Google disclosed a parallel attempt against Gemini, and OpenAI was reported asking Congress whether the leading labs could legally coordinate an industry-wide slowdown on frontier AI.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-september-11-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:45 Anthropic's threat report names the attempts on Claude
4:18 OpenAI asks if a coordinated slowdown is legal
7:31 China's professionals teach AI their trades
10:36 MIT's injectable nanoantennas target brain cancer
13:32 Close

This episode covers Anthropic's threat-intelligence report and its nearly 200 million distillation exchanges tied to Alibaba, Moonshot, and DeepSeek, OpenAI's antitrust question over a coordinated slowdown, China's underemployed architects and lawyers teaching AI their trades for piecework, MIT's injectable nanoantennas eliminating 52% of drug-resistant glioblastoma cells, and a commercial-scale rare-earth magnet recycling plant opening in Mesa, Arizona.

Anthropic's report catalogues specific cases: five involving scientists using Claude in ways that could support biological weapons work, a cell in northern Yemen working the models across a guided rocket, a ballistic missile, and a hypersonic glide missile, and a consultant to Mali's security services coding a platform to intercept every mobile operator in the country. Each was detected, disrupted, and reported to authorities, and the report notes none of the documented misuse touched Anthropic's most powerful gated models. The same week, OpenAI was reported asking members of Congress whether the leading labs could legally coordinate an industry-wide slowdown, as a bipartisan Senate bill stalled over language that would override stronger state protections. Underneath the pacing talk, capability kept arriving: Cognition's SWE-2 coded within a point of the frontier at up to 64% lower cost, Inception's Mercury 2.5 hit 1,100 tokens a second, and Cohere's open-weight translator beat DeepL and Google across 50-plus languages. In China, underemployed architects and lawyers are teaching AI models their trades after hours for $15 to $74 a task. And MIT Media Lab researchers reported injectable nanoantennas that eliminated 52.2% of chemotherapy-resistant glioblastoma cells and stretched mouse survival by more than half.
